reconstructed_theorem_text: For every real inner-product normed vector space H, every natural N>0, every real lambda, every phi:R->H, vectors v,a,y:H, and t:R, assume phi has derivative v at t. Put n=(N:R) and r(s)=n^(-1) times (a+phi(s))-y. Then s->norm(r(s))^2 has derivative (2/n)*inner_product(r(t),v) at t, and s->(n/lambda)*norm(r(s))^2 has derivative (2/lambda)*inner_product(r(t),v) at the same t. Only differentiability of phi at t is supplied; both displayed real derivatives are derived. All parameters except s remain fixed. No completeness, finite dimensionality, or global differentiability is assumed. Lambda is arbitrary, including zero and negative values. Real division is totalized with inverse(0)=0: at lambda=0 the second function is identically zero and its stated derivative is zero, while the first statement is unchanged. N=0 is excluded explicitly.
objects: H; positive natural N; arbitrary real lambda; vector-valued curve phi; derivative vector v; fixed vectors a,y; point t; two real squared-norm functions.
domains: H has NormedAddCommGroup and InnerProductSpace R structures, with no CompleteSpace hypothesis. phi:R->H; v,a,y:H; s,t,lambda:R; N:N with N>0.
quantifiers: Universally quantify H and its structures, N>0, lambda, phi,v,a,y,t. HasDerivAt(phi,v,t) implies the conjunction of the two HasDerivAt conclusions at t.
assumptions: The given space structures, N>0, and phi having genuine scalar-parameter derivative v at t. There is no sign or nonzero condition on lambda and no supplied differentiability of either squared-norm function.
conclusion: With r(s)=(N:R)^(-1) times (a+phi(s))-y, the derivatives at t of norm(r(s))^2 and ((N:R)/lambda)*norm(r(s))^2 exist and equal (2/(N:R))*inner_product(r(t),v) and (2/lambda)*inner_product(r(t),v), respectively.
scopes: Only s varies. In particular a and y are fixed vectors, so no derivatives of them occur. The hypothesis concerns one point t rather than global or continuous differentiability. At lambda=0 totalized division makes the second function and derivative zero. No measure or probabilistic interpretation is part of the claim.
constant_dependencies: The literal derivative factors are 2/(N:R) and 2/lambda. The residual depends on N,a,y,phi(t), and the inner product additionally on v. Cancellation of N in the second coefficient uses N>0 and does not require lambda nonzero.
